title: KeyScale
description: A key track and a free 12-note scale remap. T9's note trigs set the key (note - 60, C5) and still play (silence T9 with its SRC channel); while T9 is muted the key holds; the key is added to the notes of the tracks with transpose on, then the scale table remaps each note's pitch class on the tracks with scale on. FUNC + TRIG opens stock Quantize; pressed again it opens the overlay (and again goes back to Quantize). On T9 the overlay is the scale editor: two drawn keyboards (inputs, and outputs showing unused and doubled notes, and a dot on the last note played through the scale); hold a trig key as the source and press another to set its output (trigs 9-16 white keys, 2 3 5 6 7 black), knobs A-H: C..G, UP/DOWN step through three pages: page 1 has the last four keys plus E (selected note's output), F (selection), G (wrap note, where the remap window starts, C by default) and H (KeyScale off for all tracks: an OFF screen, H turns it back on); page 2 has the first eight keys; page 3 has the slots: four user slots and the CMAJ / GMIN presets, UP/DOWN to pick one, LEFT/RIGHT for LOAD/SAVE, YES to do it (loading the active slot again reverts); on any other track it opens that track's SCALE / TRANSPOSE switches (knobs A, B) and its last fired note, in > out, with TRN / SCL lit when transpose or the scale moved it. FUNC + TRIG 1-16 moves the overlay to that track without leaving it (the active track stays). NO closes. The key resets to 0 on stop. The per-track switches are kept per pattern, in T9's CC4-CC8 values. The table, wrap note, on/off and user slots are saved (eMMC block 0x6004e).
